beats.care: See a caged palapitta? Report it on the toll-free line 18004255364 or dial 112. Watching one fly free is the real tradition.
beats.what: Police Commissioner VC Sajjanar urged people not to capture, cage or sell palapittas, after reports of birds with clipped wings.
beats.why: Seeing a palapitta at Dasara is an old tradition, and some people trap the birds to show them off for money.

cards.body: Sajjanar pointed out that the bird eats insects and pests that damage crops, so it quietly helps farmers.
The bird looks dull when perched, but flashes bright blue when it opens its wings in flight.

cards.q: Have you seen a palapitta at Dasara?

opts: It is a rare pet breed
cards.q: Why is catching a palapitta a problem?
cards.why: As a protected wild species under the Wildlife Act, it is illegal to capture, cage or trade it.

hook: Caged *palapittas* at Dasara? Police say it can land you in trouble

learn.t: The palapitta, or Indian roller, is Telangana's state bird and is protected under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

tldr: Hyderabad's police chief asked people not to catch, cage or sell the palapitta, Telangana's state bird, in the name of Dasara.
